name: Shammua (son of Zaccur, spy from the tribe of Reuben)
title: Spy from the tribe of Reuben
summary: Shammua, son of Zaccur, was the representative from the tribe of Reuben among the twelve spies that Moses sent to explore the land of Canaan. He was one of the ten spies who returned with a negative report and discouraged the Israelites from entering the land. As a result of their lack of faith, this generation was condemned to wander in the wilderness for forty years.

keyEvents.title: Chosen as a Spy
keyEvents.description: Moses chose Shammua, son of Zaccur, as the representative of the tribe of Reuben to scout out the land of Canaan at the Lord's command.

keyEvents.title: The Spying Mission in Canaan
keyEvents.description: Shammua was among the twelve spies who explored the land of Canaan for forty days from the Desert of Sin to Rehob near Lebo-Hamath.

keyEvents.title: The Negative Report
keyEvents.description: Shammua was among the ten spies who gave a discouraging report to the people, saying that the inhabitants of the land were too strong to be overcome, which spread fear among the Israelites.

keyEvents.title: The People's Rebellion
keyEvents.description: The negative report from Shammua and the other spies caused the entire congregation to break out in cries of complaint and want to choose a new leader to return to Egypt.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on the Unfaithful Spies
keyEvents.description: God punished the ten spies who had spread a bad report about the land. Shammua and the other unfaithful spies died by a plague before the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Judgment on the Generation
keyEvents.description: As a result of the lack of faith triggered by the spies' report, the entire generation over twenty years old was condemned to wander in the wilderness for forty years without entering the promised land.
